title: UNESCO Inscribes Sarnath (Uttar Pradesh) as India's 45th World Heritage Site
summary: Inscribed at 48th World Heritage Committee session in Busan; includes Dhamekh & Chaukhandi Stupas.

blocks.content: Inscribed at 48th World Heritage Committee session in Busan; includes Dhamekh & Chaukhandi Stupas.

items: World Heritage Site: Sarnath inscribed as India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site (Criteria iii & vi).
Monuments Included: Chaukhandi Stupa, Dhamekh Stupa, Dharmarajika Stupa, Mulagandhakuti Vihara, and Ashokan Pillar (Lion Capital).
Global Ranking: India ranks 6th globally and 2nd in Asia-Pacific for total UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

blocks.quote:
Interview Focus Question: "What is the historical significance of Sarnath's UNESCO World Heritage inscription?"
💡 **Model Answer: Sarnath is where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta); the site houses the Ashokan Lion Capital, which forms India's official National Emblem.**
